https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/tin-can/34114e0.description: ABOUT TIN CAN Tin Can is building a safer, simpler way for kids to connect — without smartphones. We're creating screen-free, delightful devices and services that let families call the people who matter most, free from the noise of today's digital world. We're building a bold, authentic, nostalgic, and kinda quirky brand that resonates with folks who want something simpler & better for their kids than the tech-infused lives we're currently living (and who have a sense of humor about it). As we gear up to scale to thousands of families, we're ready to bring on a designer to help make it happen. THE ROLE Kids want a phone that just works. Parents want to know exactly what it's doing. Designing for both, at once, without either one feeling like an afterthought — that's the role. We're looking for a Principal UX Designer to own the experience of Tin Can from a family's first consideration to their eight millionth call. That means the app parents live in (contacts, quiet hours, their whole relationship with the device) and it means onboarding and retention, the moments that turn a new box on the counter into something a family can't imagine living without. This isn't just a design-what's-asked-of-you role. You'll run research to understand what's actually working and what isn't, partnering with Product to figure out what to do next, not just how to build it. You'll work closely with the Head of Product, Engineering, and Brand so that software, hardware, and brand feel like one coherent product rather than a set of one-offs. This is a hands-on senior IC role: You'll do the design work yourself, and you'll establish the patterns, flows, and design language that let us scale design deliberately, including with AI, over time. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Own design across the whole software experience, shaping the core Tin Can experience, the stuff that keeps the phone ringing - Run research yourself, talk to families, watch where things break, to set your next move - Shape what we build next, not just how; you're a strategic thought partner to Product, not just an executor - Build the patterns and design language that help the team and when appropriate, AI, move fast but meet our bar - Get hands-on: prototype it, write the copy, sit with an engineer until it’s right WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - 10+ years designing and shipping consumer digital products, with clear examples of owning complex experiences end to end - Excellent visual design craft, with a gift for making complex workflows feel simple - A strong systems thinker who builds reusable foundations, not just one-off screens - A strategic partner to Product who shapes what we build next, not just how - Fluency using AI as a design multiplier (exploration, prototyping, production), and genuine interest in building a foundation the team can scale with it - Excellent judgment around user trust, safety, and quality, especially designing for kids and the parents who trust us - Ability to set direction and move independently, with little oversight - Hands-on and scrappy approach; you'd rather build the component or run the test yourself than wait on someone else - Low-ego and collaborative vibes; you share credit and pitch in on problems that aren't yours WHY JOIN TIN CAN - We're building tech that protects childhood: We're on a quest to give kids a more analog childhood — one with real conversations, real connection, and way less screen time. No doomscrolling, data mining, or dopamine traps — just a simpler, better way for kids to stay in touch. This is a rare opportunity to build something that truly matters. - You'll set the foundation, not inherit one: As our first dedicated UX owner, you'll define how the software experience looks, feels, and scales — with the autonomy and backing of the founding team to do it right. - Small, high-trust team: Every company says "team," but at Tin Can it means something different. We're a small, mission-driven group that genuinely has each other's backs — professionally and personally. You'll be joining a tight-knit crew where your ideas and instincts matter from day one. - Room to explore, not just execute: You'll have the space to explore new ideas, challenge assumptions, and shape an experience that reflects our values of trust, simplicity, and care. If you're excited by the idea of shaping how thousands of families experience something simpler and better for their kids, please reach out. We can't wait to meet someone who's ready to jump in, set the bar, and help us grow.

More resources to learn about our work: Our Research blog - covering advances including Monosemantic Features and Circuits An Intro to Interpretability from our research lead, Chris Olah The Urgency of Interpretability from CEO Dario Amodei Engineering Challenges Scaling Interpretability - directly relevant to this role 60 Minutes segment - see a demo of tooling our team built New Yorker article - what it's like to work on one of AI's hardest open problems This role is an early hire on a new infrastructure effort within Interpretability: you'll help define its charter, not just execute it. Your job is to build the paved path that makes that access secure by default, private by design, and low-friction for every researcher. The work spans four areas: Security: design the secure-by-default environments and access patterns that enable deep model access for an organization whose research requires it - done well, the same design improves both our security posture and research productivity. Privacy: build data-access patterns that ensure policy adherence as our research moves from theory into practical application Data & Compute Management: manage research data at petabyte scale and make efficient use of large accelerator fleets - storage lifecycle, capacity planning, and scheduling. Developer experience: agentic engineering, tooling and observability that keep researchers moving fast In this role, you’ll be deeply embedded alongside Interp Researchers to understand their workflows - building your understanding of the research as you go; at the same time you’ll bridge communication with Anthropic’s wider platform and security teams.. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research.
